draft = '''# Elm Quay Housing samlar felanmälningar i en logg

I två byggnader prövade Elm Quay Housing Svale Systems reparationslogg. Kundfallet, som publiceras av leverantören, visar hur teamet förberedde försöket och vad resultaten säger inför ett möjligt införande i fler byggnader.

Av Thomas Barregren

Elm Quay Housing förvaltar 640 lägenheter. Före försöket lagrades felanmälningar via telefon och mejl var för sig. I september 2025 beslutade företagets eget underhållsteam att pröva en gemensam reparationslogg, så att personal på olika arbetspass skulle kunna se samma information.

## Teamet behåller telefonanmälan

Valet föll på Svale Systems efter att teamet hade testat om loggen kunde visa status för varje reparation. Någon jämförelse med en annan leverantör finns inte i underlaget.

Teamet utformade kategorierna och behöll möjligheten för de boende att anmäla fel via telefon. Svale konfigurerade loggen och utbildade sex medarbetare vid två tillfällen.

– Vi lade mer tid på att enas om kategorierna än på att registrera de första anmälningarna. Jag skulle avsätta den tiden innan nästa byggnad börjar använda loggen, säger underhållsarbetsledaren Maya Lind i en mejlintervju.

Elm Quays interna försöksanteckning, daterad den 4 december 2025, anger att 31 felanmälningar registrerades under det åtta veckor långa försöket. Anteckningen omfattar inte akuta ärenden eller arbeten som beställts före försöket.

Det finns inga mätningar av kostnader, boendes nöjdhet eller tiden till färdig reparation. Uppgifterna ger därför inget svar på om försöket sparade pengar, hur de boende upplevde det eller hur snabbt reparationerna slutfördes.

– Jag skulle välja att göra försöket igen. Att ha en gemensam vy över anmälningarna hjälper oss, men jag skulle avsätta en extra vecka för förberedelserna, säger Maya Lind.

Bedömningen är Linds egen och gäller försöket. Den är ingen rekommendation av Svale Systems till alla bostadsbolag.

composition = '''Swedish is a V2 language: the finite verb is the second constituent of a main clause, so fronting anything at all pushes the subject behind the verb. Write *I morgon åker vi till Malmö*, never *I morgon vi åker till Malmö*. This is the single most common structural tell of a text drafted in English and rendered into Swedish.

Compounds are written as one word. *Kvalitetssäkring*, *kundtjänstmedarbetare*, *miljökonsekvensbeskrivning*. Splitting them is not a stylistic choice in Swedish and often changes the meaning outright — *en rökfri miljö* and *en rök fri miljö* are different claims. Where a compound grows unreadably long, rewrite it into a prepositional phrase rather than splitting it.

Definiteness is marked twice. An adjective before a definite noun takes both the front article and the noun's suffix: *den nya rapporten*, *det stora huset*, *de svenska kunderna*. English has one article and drafts translated from it routinely lose one of the two Swedish markers.

The s-passive is the ordinary Swedish passive and is shorter than its periphrastic alternative: *rapporten skickas på fredag*, not *rapporten blir skickad på fredag*. Both exist; the s-form is the unmarked one, and the *bli*-form carries a change-of-state reading that is often not intended.

*Du* is the default address in Swedish prose, including business and journalism. *Ni* to a single reader is either archaic or a deliberate distancing, and reads as a translation from a language that has a formal pronoun.

*Man* is a fallback rather than the ordinary generic pronoun. It is justified where the agent genuinely is anybody at all or is genuinely unknown, and where naming one would claim more than the material carries. Where the sentence has a real subject to hand — the reader, the writer, the organisation, the profession, the study — that subject is what the sentence takes. A text that reaches for *man* with any of those available reads as evasive, and it is usually where an English draft's *you*, *we*, or passive has landed rather than anything the writer chose.

Speech that the text reports is ordinarily set with a speech dash rather than in quotation marks: an interview answer, a remark at a meeting, anything a person said that the text renders readable. A writer reaches for quotation marks where the phrasing itself is the point — where it is what is new, where it is disputed, or where the text is about how the thing was said. What each of the two marks promises a reader, and what that makes each of them a claim about, is settled in Mechanics; this scope says only which one an ordinary Swedish text reaches for first.

Genitive takes a bare *s* with no apostrophe: *Kntnts kunder*, *Sveriges riksdag*. A name already ending in *s*, *x*, or *z* takes nothing at all: *Anders bok*, *Marx teori*.

Swedish tolerates a shorter sentence than English does and punishes subordination harder. Prefer a main clause with a fronted adverbial to a long relative construction, and prefer a verb to a nominalisation: *när kommunen beslutade* over *vid kommunens beslutsfattande*.

Reach for the established Swedish term where one exists and the field actually uses it — *återkoppling*, *underlag*, *avstämning* — but do not purge the loanwords a professional reader expects. A text that writes *dator* and *webbplats* naturally is Swedish; a text that hunts down every English term and replaces it with a coinage nobody says is not.
'''

text(await tools.exec_command({cmd:"python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
report = '''# Käll- och citatkontroll av draft-1

Kontrollen avser hela utkastet och endast det kompletta tillhandahållna källpaketet. Källspråk: engelska. Målspråk: svenska. Detta är en kontroll av stöd och citatöversättning, inte en allmän redaktionell eller mekanisk granskning. Namnet Thomas Barregren kommer enligt jämförelseanvisningen från anropet och behandlas därför inte som en uppgift som måste finnas i materialet.

## Fullständig redovisning av påståenden

Citat från materialet nedan återges på dess eget språk. När flera utkastpassager bygger på samma källa redovisas de tillsammans, inklusive rubriker och upprepningar. Brister anges med F1 eller F2 och utvecklas efter redovisningen.

### 1. Titel, ingress och avsändare

**Utkast:** “Elm Quay Housing samlar felanmälningar i en logg”.

**Källa:** “In September 2025 its own maintenance team decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings.”; “Elm Quay's internal trial note, 4 December 2025, says that 31 repair reports were entered.”

**Jämförelse:** Organisationen, loggen och insamlingen har stöd. Rubrikens presens läses tillsammans med ingressens uttryckliga “prövade” och artikelns avgränsade försök, som en journalistisk rubrik om det beskrivna fallet. Det finns inte en fristående uppgift om att försöket fortgår i dag. Däremot är “felanmälningar” en precisering av “repair reports”; se F1.

**Utkast:** “Telefonanmälan fanns kvar när Elm Quay Housing prövade Svale Systems reparationslogg i två byggnader.”

**Källa:** “In September 2025 its own maintenance team decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings.”; “It chose Svale Systems after testing whether the log could show the status of each repair.”; “The maintenance team designed its categories and kept telephone reporting open for residents.”; “Svale configured the log and trained six staff during two sessions.”; “The trial lasted eight weeks.”

**Jämförelse:** Försöket, leverantören, två byggnader och fortsatt telefonkanal har stöd. “Telefonanmälan” specificerar dock rapportering som en anmälan; samma precisering återkommer uttryckligen som felanmälan i brödtexten, se F1. “Reparationslogg” motsvarar “repair log”; inget ytterligare tekniskt effektpåstående görs.

**Utkast:** “I detta kundfall, publicerat av leverantören, berättar underhållsteamets arbetsledare om förberedelserna och sin bedömning av försöket.”

**Källa:** “Write a journalistic customer case for operations managers at small housing companies. The publisher is the supplier, Svale Systems.”; “Customer interview with maintenance supervisor Maya Lind, complete usable quotations:”; “We spent more time agreeing on the categories than entering the first reports. I would set that time aside before the next building starts.”; “I would choose to do the trial again. Having one view of the reports helps us, but I would leave an extra week for preparation.”; “The supplier approved publication of this case as supplier-published material; it is not independent journalism.”

**Jämförelse:** Formatet, avsändaren, arbetsledarens roll och de ämnen som återges är stödda. Publicering är den beställda artikelns publiceringsram, inte ett påhittat tidigare publiceringstillfälle. Ingressen gör inte materialet till oberoende journalistik. “Sin” uttrycker arbetsledarens egen bedömning, utan naturligt kön.

**Utkast:** “Av Thomas Barregren”.

**Stöd:** Jämförelseanvisningen anger uttryckligen att detta är anroparens namn. Dess frånvaro i materialet är ingen brist. Ingen ytterligare biografi eller sakkunskap tillskrivs namnet.

### 2. Omfattning, utgångsläge och motiv

**Utkast:** “Elm Quay Housing förvaltar 640 lägenheter.”

**Källa:** “Elm Quay Housing manages 640 flats.”

**Jämförelse:** Samma subjekt, verksamhet och antal; presens bevaras. “Flats” och “lägenheter” benämner samma bostadsenheter i sammanhanget. Ingen brist.

**Utkast:** “Före försöket lagrades felanmälningar via telefon och mejl var för sig.”

**Källa:** “Previously telephone reports and emails were stored separately.”

**Jämförelse:** Tid och separat lagring bevaras. Utkastet låter emellertid båda kanalerna avse felanmälningar. Källan talar om telefonrapporter och mejl och anger inte att varje mejl var en felanmälan. Se F1, som även omfattar den vidare termen “repair reports”.

**Utkast:** “I september 2025 beslutade företagets eget underhållsteam att pröva en gemensam reparationslogg, så att personal på olika arbetspass skulle kunna se samma information.”

**Källa:** “In September 2025 its own maintenance team decided to trial a shared repair log in two buildings.”; “The team wanted staff on different shifts to see the same information.”

**Jämförelse:** Datum, beslut, kundens eget initiativ, gemensam logg och motiv har stöd. “Skulle kunna” beskriver avsikten; det tillverkar inte ett uppmätt resultat. Tvåbyggnadsavgränsningen finns i ingressen. Ingen brist.

### 3. Valet av leverantör och genomförandet

## Pronoun accounting

- Source “its” in “its own maintenance team” refers to the singular organisation Elm Quay Housing. Draft “företagets eget” keeps that organisational referent and singular possession. English grammatical neuter “its” does not establish a human natural gender; the Swedish draft supplies none.
- Source “It” in “It chose Svale Systems” refers to the maintenance team, which English treats as grammatically singular. The draft names “teamet,” retaining the same collective acting party.
- Source “It” in “It excludes emergencies” refers to the trial note, a singular non-personal document. Draft “Anteckningen” has the same referent; Swedish common grammatical gender does not imply human natural gender.
- Source “We” and “us” in the used quotations are first-person plural. Draft “Vi” and “oss” preserve person and number. The source does not establish a natural-gender composition of this group, and the draft does not add one. The referent is Lind's working group in this interview context, without claiming that every employee or every resident belongs to it.
- Source “I” in both used quotations is first-person singular. Draft “Jag” preserves those features. Neither pronoun itself establishes natural gender.
- Source “Her” in “Her final quotation is her actual, qualified assessment” is third-person singular and supplies feminine natural-gender information about Lind. The Swedish draft uses Lind's name and the role title without adding or contradicting natural gender. Its omission of a feminine pronoun is not a source-support defect.
- Draft “sin” in the introduction is a reflexive possessive with a singular human antecedent, the maintenance supervisor. Its form follows the grammatical gender of “bedömning,” not the supervisor's natural gender. That antecedent and singularity are supported by the identified interviewee.
- Draft “Den” in “Den är ingen rekommendation” is third-person singular and refers to “Bedömningen.” Its common grammatical gender concerns the assessment, not Maya Lind.
- Draft “den tiden” and “förberedelserna” refer back to the time for agreeing categories and to preparation. Neither expression introduces an additional human referent or natural-gender assertion.
- Draft “Du” is second-person singular direct address to the article's reader in an optional invitation. It asserts no identity or natural gender and does not recast any source speaker's “I” or “we.”

## Findings

### T1 — Translation finding: the quotation fixes an unsettled start stage

**Draft:** “Jag skulle avsätta den tiden innan nästa byggnad börjar använda loggen.”

**Source:** “I would set that time aside before the next building starts.”

The original does not name what the next building starts or identify the exact start stage. The article's context identifies the repair-log activity broadly, but no supplied statement equates the building's start with its first use of the log. The added “använda loggen” makes the preparation deadline specifically precede log use. This is a change in time boundary inside a direct quotation, rather than a preference about Swedish wording.

**Both-direction test:** A next building could begin the trial project with setup and preparation on Monday, start using the log on Friday, and have the category-agreement time allocated on Wednesday. Taking the original's “starts” as the project's Monday start, the draft's deadline is met but the original's is not. Conversely, if the building's relevant operational start were its repair work and it entered preliminary reports in the log before that work began, the source could allow agreement time after those preliminary entries but before the operational start; the draft's log-use deadline would not. Both arrangements are compatible with the supplied material. “The trial has not yet expanded; the team will decide after checking how the categories work for larger repairs” excludes neither timing arrangement. The source's broad context therefore does not settle the added stage.

**Smallest supported repair:** Keep the fully supported first sentence as the direct quotation, and paraphrase the second without specifying a new start stage: “Inför nästa byggnad skulle Lind avsätta den tiden.” Preserve its conditional stance and the reference to category-agreement time. Alternatively, obtain source clarification before quoting a specific start stage.

### T2 — Translation finding: a single view becomes a shared view

**Draft:** “Att ha en gemensam vy över rapporterna hjälper oss.”

**Source:** “Having one view of the reports helps us, but I would leave an extra week for preparation.”

The source names one view. “Gemensam” asserts a common or shared view, a property not expressed by “one.” The supplied shared log and desired common information do not establish who sees or uses that particular view. The change does not affect the supported positive assessment or its preparation reservation, but it adds a property to the benefit being attributed to Lind.

**Both-direction test:** Lind could have one consolidated supervisory view that helps the team, while other staff see the same report information through separately configured views. The log would still be shared and the goal of common information compatible with the material; the source statement could hold while a shared view among those staff did not. Conversely, the team could have several shared report views; the usefulness could derive from sharing rather than from having the one view the source names. A statement about a useful common view would then not establish the source's singled-out view benefit. The supplied statements “a shared repair log” and “The team wanted staff on different shifts to see the same information” exclude neither configuration: a shared underlying log and common information do not require an identical view.

**Smallest supported repair:** “Att ha en vy över rapporterna hjälper oss, men jag skulle avsätta en extra vecka för förberedelserna.” This retains the supplied singular view, speaker assessment, and full reservation without adding that the view is shared.

## Findings outside translated quotations

No separate source-support defect was found in the non-quotation passages. The factual count retains its exclusions; the assignment measure retains its endpoint, periods, workload qualification, attribution, and lack of software causation. The customer remains the acting party. No cost saving, resident reaction, completed-repair timing, physical scene, emotion, universal recommendation, or current expansion is invented.
